text:
maria: Heads-up — traffic forecast for eu-west shows an expected 2.8x spike this Sat 00:00-06:00 UTC due to the partner promo. Current proposal: bump burst_cap to 18% of pool, reduce holdback to 6%, shorten reserve_window to 60s. Thoughts?

maria: Quick numbers so we're aligned: current steady GPU-hours ~1200h/day; expected peak-day ~3200h (+~2000h). If we lean on burst we risk hitting preemptible quotas in fallback regions (us-west).

lee: I don't love lowering holdback under 10%. Last time we did <8% we had cascading scheduling delays and some 503s during scale-down. :thinking_face:

aj: Agree with lee. Alternative config that kept us stable in sim:
```yaml
autoscaler: 
  min_replicas: 30
  burst_cap_pct: 12
  holdback_pct: 10
  reserve_window_ms: 120000
  hysteresis_sec: 90
```
This limits spike throttle while keeping reserve window long enough to avoid flapping.

devops-bot: [autoscale-runbook] forecast_alert created for spike >2x. Notifying #oncall and adding ephemeral reservation request.

kai: Also consider region routing tweaks: temporarily route non-SLA traffic to eu-central and fallback to on-prem for batch workloads. We can do ~15% spillover to eu-central with minimal p99 latency change.

shelby: Cost check — quick calc shows: temporary reserved add (50 GPUs for 8h) ~ $18k (one-off), relying on burst + preemptible swap could be unpredictably higher (~$25-30k) if we need cross-region egress and spinups. Reserved for the promo might be cheaper and safer.

natalie: Dashboard snapshot: https://dash.internal/redwood/infra/autoscale?view=eu-west (watch the scalers tab). Last similar promo (2025-11-07) we saw sustained queue depth for 12m and submit latency p95 jump ~2.4x.

oncall-bot: oncall rotation: @maria oncall for UTC 22:00-08:00. I can escalate if anything crosses 80% scheduling failures.

maria: Proposal v2 then: set burst_cap to 15%, holdback to 8%, reserve_window to 60s, and provision 50 reserved GPUs from 23:00-07:00 UTC for eu-west. We'll also enable cross-region spill to eu-central at 15% for non-SLA traffic.

aj: If we're provisioning reserved, we should also patch the autoscaler to avoid preemptible fallbacks until reserve is active (short lock window). I'll draft a small change: `autoscaler.behaviors.prevent_preemptible_fallback = true` for the window.

lee: +1 for preventing fallback while reserved pool is filling. Also add a smoothing rule: only allow scale-down if observed average < 0.6 for 5m. Prevents premature scale-down during burst tail.

maria: I'll schedule the reserved request now and post the terraform change for autoscaler/burst_policy.tf. If no objections by 16:00 UTC I'll apply.

kai: :thumbsup:

shelby: I'll run a quick cost delta and give a final number by 15:30 UTC.

natalie: I'll put live monitors on the scalers + schedule an eval of p95/p99 for the rollout window.

oncall-bot: Reminder: runbook step 4 requires a manual check of GPU driver versions on prewarmed hosts before turning traffic up.

maria: thanks — will follow the checklist.

aj: terraform plan output (partial):
```
Plan: 1 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.
+ resource "reserved_gpu_allocation" "promo_eu_west" { count = 1 }
~ resource "autoscaler_policy" "eu_burst" { burst_cap_pct: 12 -> 15 }
```

lee: Good. Keep an eye on the BGP flaps — last promo we saw a short network blip when we hit the interconnect threshold. Notify network team if we start to push cross-region >20%.

maria: noted. I'll ping network if we breach 15% cross-region traffic. Applying changes at 23:30 if everything looks green.

aj: I'll be on-call for rollout and ready to rollback the autoscaler patch if we see scheduling errors.

maria: ok — thanks everyone.
